item.title: Introducing Skills on Best of AI
item.description:
We just shipped something new: Skills, a section of the directory built for finding Agent Skills.

What are Skills?

If you’re working with Claude or another LLM agent, you’ve probably seen how a good “Skill” (a packaged set of instructions, scripts, and best practices) can turn a generic model into something that handles a specific job really well: editing Word docs, running test-driven development, reviewing a pull request, building a polished frontend.

item.title: New Feature: AI Companies
item.description:
Best of AI has always been organized around tools: one page per product, grouped into categories and professions. That answers “what should I use for X,” not “who’s behind this.” Today we’re adding the other half: Companies, a directory of the labs and businesses building the tools you already browse here.

What’s on a company page

Each of the 500 companies we’ve added so far gets its own page: founding year, headquarters, founders, a short description of what they actually build, and a link to every one of their tools already listed on Best of AI. Open the OpenAI page and you’ll see ChatGPT, DALL-E, and the rest of their lineup pulled in automatically.

item.title: Best of AI is now open source!
item.description:
We started Best of AI about a year ago as a curated list of AI tools worth using. Today the whole thing is open source on GitHub — data, site, scripts, CI. Community-driven from here on out.

Flat files, no database

Every tool is a Markdown file in content/tools/. Categories live in data/categories.yaml. The leaderboard ranks tools from data/leaderboard.yaml. No Postgres, no headless CMS, no vendor lock-in. Clone the repo, git grep for what you need, send a PR when something’s wrong. That’s the whole model.
